beats.text: The villain is the blank slate. It treats every environment as a new mystery, wasting cycles guessing instead of building a persistent reality.
beats.visual_focus: A split screen showing a chaotic search tree versus a structured rulebook.

beats.text: Memento 3 pivots by externalizing memory. It maintains a natural-language rulebook, treating environment dynamics as revisable hypotheses rather than static weights.

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: This actually slapped. You didn't waste my time with 'Today we're going to look at' or some cringe 'digital brain' metaphor. You got straight to the point about why LLMs suck at logic—the lack of persistent state—and explained the fix as a compilation process. It feels like a real dev talking to another dev. I'm actually interested in how the 'strict judge' handles the code validation.
